speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe your age and how long you have been experiencing these symptoms. To help narrow this down, do you notice any drooping of your eyelids or changes in your speech or swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That pattern of weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest is very characteristic; do you experience significant muscle weakness in your bulbar muscles, such as difficulty chewing, swallowing, or speaking clearly? Also, does lifting your arms to your shoulders cause noticeable fatigue?

REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR antibodies, Anti-MuSK antibodies, and Anti-striational antibodies.
REQUEST IMAGES: EMG_Neurophysiology

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Anti-AChR antibodies: Present (elevated); Anti-MuSK antibodies: Not detected; Anti-striational antibodies: Not detected; EMG_Neurophysiology: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Patient
text: The weakness is clearly worse with exertion and better after rest. I have not noticed muscle wasting or weight loss. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis.

The mention of Tuberculosis is likely a misinterpretation by your previous physician, as your symptoms of fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest are classic for Myasthenia Gravis, an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction. The antibodies we ordered should confirm this; if they are negative, we will need to look for other causes like Lambert-Eaton or a central nervous system issue.
